The *Sāsavaduka* (Patthana 8.15) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* ("Conditional Relations"), the final book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Designated as a leaf section in the canon, it systematically applies conditional relations to the dyad (*duka*) of phenomena accompanied by cankers or taints (*sāsava*) [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records no modern translations or curated external parallels for this section [SuttaCentral]. However, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal alignment, registering 139 matching passages across 43 other Pali texts, virtually all of which reside in parallel divisions of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. The most significant overlaps occur with other sections analyzing cankers (*āsava*), including the *Āsavagocchaka* in the *Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.4; 6 matches), the *Kusalattika, Āsavaparāmāsagocchaka* (Patthana 4.4; 8 matches), the *Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 20.3; 6 matches), the *Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 2.3; 8 matches), and the related dyad *Āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka* (Patthana 8.19; 5 matches), as well as the *Āsavaduka* (Patthana 8.14) and *Āsavasāsavaduka* (Patthana 14.16) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are identified above the threshold score [DharmaNexus].
